In the Hibryds Cinematic Universe, there is a separate system called a Beast Hierarchy Kingdom, where it classifies each creatures' strengths and where they are in the ranks of the kingdom.
Werebels, aka Were Rabbits, also called Killer Rabbits, are bipedal mutations of sterilized rabbits that are escapees of illicit vampire experimentations.
Through time, Werebels only sought power and strength, and it was classified in 1607 AD that they are Apex Beasts of the Beast Kingdom.

Deeragons primarily live on Norrane, but they travel freely around the world to breed and expand their race.
The fur coating on their neck and their wings keeps their body warm and soft, as they like basking in the sunlight.
The Demon Race is one of the most misunderstood and most underestimated cultures on Planet Hetra.
At their cultural core, demons are a personification of beauty, wealth, and knowledge, not merely the raw strength that places them at the top of the Beast Hierarchy Kingdom.
Food is one of the quieter but more telling expressions of demon culture.

One of the most well-known dishes made by Lesser Demons, Dàema Énchil Curry is a slow-prepared curry with roots in the culinary traditions of demon communities that lived across Varleqe and its surrounding territories.
The dish is known for its deceptively light texture offset by a rich, layered spiciness that builds gradually on the palate.
The spice is never described as harsh or overwhelming; it sits at a precise threshold that warms without punishing, enriched with depth that most non-demon cooks struggle to replicate.

The scent of Dàema Énchil Curry cooking outdoors is said to carry far enough to attract wildlife, which is considered a quiet mark of quality in demon culinary tradition, as even the natural world recognizes something worth gathering for.
The spoken language of demon culture is Varnæn, the Demonic dialect of ancient Ghrenglish.
Verbs carry endings like -nuhl, -aem, and -farg, and the dialect is heavy with glottal breaks and sounds like "sk," "dr," "gh," and "kh."
Embedded within it are strong cultural taboos, most notably the phrase Skærøl Ǧhrün'pæarou, a deeply offensive insult that loosely translates to "a deformed child from their mother's womb."
Varnæn is also mutually respected by Sylphic Ghrenglish (Aeþerlen) speakers.
Scholars from both language traditions have long been friends, and both dialects borrow from each other in moments of raw emotional honesty.
Originally sung by demons in the Varnæn dialect, the chant is not about dominance or war.
Werebels and Moonbels are known to actively hate the chant, as they break the very codes it stands for.
The church has served for millennia as a neutral territorial zone, a space where demon factions, often in conflict with one another, could gather for rites of passage, truces, and communal ceremony.
Attacking within its walls is considered a serious violation of demon cultural law, a status that has held, imperfectly but consistently, since the Greungerian Era.
Yhursa's work was so significant that the Five Giants named Yhursday (the fifth day of the Hetranian week) in her honor.
Demon culture is, in that small way, written into the very calendar of the world.
Human settlement has largely declined or collapsed here, leaving the land primarily to demons, direwolves, and beasts.
Demons have a deep, ancestral relationship with Varleqe's ancient structures, living in and around them and treating them as home territory in a way that is cultural as much as it is practical.
At the age of 23 is when demons get their abilities and powers after undergoing a process called Demonization.
The unstable cells turn into Demon Core Cells, which each develop their own unique abilities and powers.
In order to become 26 years of age, a demon has to wait for 41 years.
The actual age of a demon right now in the year of 2245 is at the age of 5,572 years old, because they all age at the same rate after their 23rd year.
Demonization is essentially hardcoded into every demon's future blood.
Demons die a horrible death, even if it means the exception of getting themselves killed by external factors. 8,999 is their oldest age until they die off into the age of 9,000.
All demon abilities and powers deteriorate their health in a span of one year, which causes them to die by the hands of too much power.
The fires of power will decrease due to low minerals in their body, and the depletion of Black Blood Cells.
The Demon Core Cells will fight over the whole body, which causes their Black Cells to die off in matter of seconds.

The power of regeneration will obviously fight back, but with little Demon Core Cell and Black Blood Cells left, that ability is left to waste and all you get is a rotten, smelly husk in their 9k years of age.
The Dragon cells override his demon cells in which he does not have The Quick Death.

Now that Planet Hetra has evolved, many fossils have been dug up throughout the course of time and have been displayed on museums.
Currently, there is no way to enter the said ruins, since the entrance is sealed off with a divine seal.

Scientists from across the continents work here to study fossil remains, conduct DNA analysis on preserved specimens, and theorize about the underground dinosaur kingdoms that may still exist beneath Hetra's surface.
Deep within H.E.L.M.S lies a restricted section called The Sealed Archives, where the most mysterious and unexplainable fossil discoveries are kept.
Access is granted only to high-level researchers and approved investigators.

Even fossils that are revived sometimes have a disability rate, which also prohibits the staff to release them to the wild.
Anything lower than that is a failure, thus the fossils are preserved as statues.

The Dregalosaurus often times breaches past the surface of the oceans to gaze out onto the land where many humans and creatures live, wondering if either instills fear towards them or they look up to said legendary creature.

In the World of Hetra, there are a lot of consumer products as of the year 2245.

The HERA Model 5 is a flagship phone from the brand HERA, known for its fantasy-inspired aesthetic and premium build quality.
The screen is generously sized, fitting comfortably in hand without feeling unwieldy.
A unique ingrained phone number comes pre-loaded into each unit, allowing free calls and messaging to anyone, anywhere in the world, at no additional cost.
The HERA MK 5 is produced by the phone brand HERALink, which is located in The District of Eldreule, Riverchnaut (Lynneria).
The Hexel LY is a sleek, holographic-enabled flagship killer built for people who live between city streets and wild trails.
The back of the phone's design has a very clear black-like metal coating, with a stylized golden trimmed V as the logo.
The Hexel LY is one of the most innovated devices as a phone with full features.
The body is a matte-anodized aluminum frame wrapped in tough, subtly textured glass, with a dark “Vexel” finish that makes the camera island and Helio emblem glow just a little when the light hits.
The front is almost all display: a bright, high-refresh LCD panel tuned for outdoor readability, with a small cutout at the top for the combined selfie/holographic module.
Inside, a custom Hexel-class chip combines CPU, GPU, and a dedicated “SmartCore” that runs the phone's intelligence entirely on the device.
The battery and thermals are tuned so you can run navigation, camera, and assistant features all day without babysitting the charger.
The internal structure can keep itself intact and self-regulated without overheating.

The real personality is the Auto-ID mode (fourth camera/tracking): point it at gear, signs, or scenery and it can recognize everyday objects, or switch into a nature-focused mode while hiking to help identify plants, animals, and fungi.
Video quality can be shot up to 8K, and photos up to 4K.
The 20,000 eXpH slim battery will not overheat or overexpand due to NiTi bones and structures.
At the software level, Hexel LY runs a custom interface built around a local, JARVIS-style assistant that you wake with a phrase like “Hey Hexel.”
You can say things like “What's my day look like?”, “Clean up my inbox,” or “Take a note and pin it here,” and get concise, characterful responses instead of rambling monologues.
You can even customize your Hexel Assistant with lots of different voices using hyper-realistic training based solely on your voice with dialogue you feed it.
You can record your voice, and Vexel will do the rest by asking you what kind of features the new voice should have.
You can even talk to Hexel natively via a Chatbot setting you can enable within the phone's settings.
The holographic transmitter and displayer is inside the selfie camera module.
The Holographic Display can even project what you want into the air, like a calendar, the weather, maps (GPS), and more.
Real membranes like ePTFE and advanced nanofiber meshes are already waterproof yet breathable, with pores much smaller than water droplets but larger than vapor, so they don't “soak” or absorb water.
Designed on the left corner of the phone, it is very small but very powerful.
Your biometric data, preferences, and assistant behavior live on the device by default, with multiple profiles gated by fingerprint, face, or both.
The assistant only sees what each profile allows, so work, personal, and guest spaces can coexist without bleeding into each other.

Eulerich is home to the Eulerians, an ancient and highly intelligent race known for their mastery of ancient technology and ancient magic.
The Eulan Kingdom is located in the Eulan Desert, sitting north of the Oelen Kingdom.
Eulanis is the major city and capital of the Eulan Kingdom.

Nestled within the Sandstone Mountains, it takes up the size of a volcanic island (comparable to Honolulu) and serves as the center for all trading posts, marketplaces, and fine goods that often come at very high prices.
Eulanis is founded and governed by King Edward Briehale and Queen Anika Briehale, two of the most prominent monarchs in Eulerich's history.
The population of Eulanis alone reaches up to 5,000 individuals, making it a compact but thriving city of commerce and governance.
The average wages reported by workers here sit around Ħ22.45 Hetrix.
Finding work under the King and Queen is not particularly difficult, as most employers continue hiring regardless of layoffs or vacations.
Orchestrated by Damien Kulvera, it was a calculated plot to kill King Renton using a rope, the Heimlich, a glass of water, and a gag.
Endriel is a thriving town located southeast of Eulanis.
Serving primarily as a trading hub, Endriel has a dedicated trading road that leads down to the Oelen Kingdom.
Earnel is a Lumberjack Town and Harbor Town located west of both Eulanis and Endriel.
The town sits near an endless supply of Dark Lumberwood Trees, which serve as the primary building material for much of Eulerich's construction and craftsmanship.
Euriel Ruins was once a thriving underground city during the ancient Eulerich Era.
The city now sits abandoned, though it remains a place of deep cultural and historical interest.
The Oelen Kingdom is located in the Oelen Plains, sitting southwest of the Eulan Kingdom.
The population of the Oelen Kingdom is estimated at around 450,340 individuals, including the king.
The kingdom was founded by King Gorvich Eckhart and Queen Fahlia Eckhart.
The Eckhart family's combined worth stands at around Ħ550 quadrillion Hetrix, just 100 quadrillion short of the Briehales.
Oelenis is the major city and capital of the Oelen Kingdom.
Located near the border of Eulerich, it takes up the size of a huge volcanic island and sits a forest's distance away from the Cold Rigid Sea.
Oelenis has active ports and ships that sail westward to the Alarctic Frost, the South Pole, for research on Alarctic Ores.
The average wages in Oelenis, as reported by well-known professions, go up to around Ħ20.65 Hetrix.
The most popular professions here are Carpentry, Smithing, Cartography, and Oceanography, reflecting the city's identity as both a mining and maritime hub.
Ol'Lenel is a thriving vintage town sitting south of Oelenis.
Every building here carries an old look but is built with a modern sensibility underneath.
Oarasel is a thriving town and village sitting northeast of Oelenis and Ol'Lenel, within the Oelen Plains.
Oarasel is a sister town to Orheigne, and the two share a close cultural and communal relationship.
Orheigne is a thriving town and village sitting southeast of Oarasel and northeast of Oelenis and Ol'Lenel.
Orehriel Ruins have since been overtaken by monsters, making any serious scholarly expedition nearly impossible.
The continent of Lynneria is one of the seven major lands on Planet Hetra.
Lynneria has two countries, one desert, and a mountain island.
All roads are confined per each district and cannot go out into the wilds.
The Wilderness contains dangerous creatures which is why Wilderness borders are fortified with Hardwood Lucid Metal infused with Hexicules.
In each district, the highways and paths are confined around their region while also passing through.
The AQTFC, also known as the Adventurer's Quarter Task Force Centre, is deployed in every district near the border.
The AQTFC is a subsidiary network of The Skypeak Obelisk, located in Grelladore.
The political map filter for Riverchnaut are shades of light violet.
Kharphan is known for famous cuisines, delicacies, and airship-tours for the city (as some buildings go as high as they go).
The District of Lenoria is made up of one huge inner city and a lot of outer towns that sit before the walled patrol border of the district.
Eldreule has technology so advanced that they developed Hyperspace Travels only towards planets within the system.
The father of science-fantasy films and other genres, with it's music having some main instruments that make up very good scores, and iconic sounds.
A heart-like shaped gulf that sits between Kharphan District and Lenoria District.
In comparison, the bridge is longer than the Great Wall of China and is the widest road in the whole world.
The bridge has up to 35 lanes with one lane for Hover Maglevs.
The political map filter for Nharvenile are shades of salmon.
Grelladore has two main attractions, the Skypeak Obelisk and the Governor's Building.
The Skypeak Obelisk is a floating tower where you can train and get experience, along with battling other power-users and gaining powers.
The main city sits in the centre of the peninsula and land, while there are western most towns that are on the peninsula like island that connects to the main land.
People often call where the main city lives as Amberwick Centre.
Before the siege though, Amberwick flourished with life, along with a secret race called Amberieans, whom have ancient knowledge from the past.
East City Harbor (EC Harbor) is a city harbor and port in Quentyn.
The wilds, the plains, the hills and the mountains here are full of wildlife.
The landscapes and sceneries are full of wonders, aside from the Wildernaught being full of dangerous creatures.
The sandy dunes here stretch miles high and wide, traversing at least one hill will take a day because the inclines up are VERY steep.
Said to contain ancient cacti and other water absorbent foliage.

Green City Harbor used to operate well with East City Harbor (a city in Nharvenile, Lynneria), but due to the massive hexicules that Norrane is made up of, the Green City Harbor was overtaken by forestation.
The Lucid Sanctum is a mysterious, enchanting place in the center of Norrane.
You can find the key on Hexphos Island, but it needs to be assembled.
Lyeceriax Fluid Spirits: Fluid Spirits can change their size but cannot alter their molecular density.
Lyecerium Crystals are what they can control, grow, and use.
Aloria was asked by Zohl to govern over a specific place that has no name yet.
Zohl told Aloria that the place she is guarding doesn't have a name yet and needs to be heavily guarded and to be created.
Thulls are magic creatures that guard the Lucid Sanctum.
Aside from swimming in bioluminescent ponds, they can survive outside of water for they have adapted to both ocean-life and land life.
The continent of Rynel sits smack-dab at the center of the globe, west of Varleqe, Hetrania, and Lynneria.
Rynel is home to six notable locations: four Oakgnar Districts that surround the Grand Tree, one sealed ruin, and one of the most economically powerful cities on Planet Hetra, New Rynels.
Rynel is also the birthplace of the Erbgeroger Flower, the sacred mountain flower that serves as the world symbol for Unity.
New Rynels is the largest coastline city in the entire world, and it takes up the entire length from the northeastern coast that stretches to the southwestern coast.
New Rynels is the wealthiest city in the entire planet of Hetra.
New Rynels was founded by Philstra Rhys, the world's first Multi-Sextillionaire, with a personal worth of 55 Sextillion Hetrix.

Philstra is the founder of many major institutions and is the primary backer of HetraSEAP, the Hetranian Space Exploration and Aeronautics Program, which alone carries a worth of around 25 quintillion Hetrix.
New Rynels is the economic powerhouse of Planet Hetra and the hub where Hetrix bills are actually minted.
Beyond finance and minting, New Rynels is a city that rewards ambition.
The District of New Rynels is split into two different regions that offer different work cultures, social activity, and more.
NWRynels is home to many famous cuisines and restaurants, along with luxury hotels and homes.
Security is still needed at the New Rynel Borders for clearance.
The Northern most wild zone that is controlled by Vernel Town of the Oakgnar District.
Vernel Wildernaughts is home to a lot of unique flowers and is also the home place for the Erbgeroger Flower within the Vernel Mountains in the north before the northern coast.
You can see the Vernel Mountain Range from any of the Oakgnar District Towns.
Sitting down on the fields and beds of grass will often feel like a hot spring because of the unique properties it has.
The Southern most wild zone that is controlled by Thimber Town of the Oakgnar District.
A rare occurrence here is that most of the blue floating lights are fireflies that light up blue instead of yellow.
The Eastern most wild zone that is controlled by Maple Town of the Oakgnar District.
The Western most wild zone that is controlled by Astel Town of the Oakgnar District.
Astel Beach never tries to take up too much space, because the landscapes of Astel Wilds are mostly dominant in terms of tourism.
In the center of the wild zone, there is a huge rock like formation that takes the shape of an hourglass.
The Oakgnar Grand District stands in the middle of the Rynel Wildernaughts.
The Oakgnar Grand Tree is composed of three main materials: a single Hexicule Core, Hardwood, and Stonewood.
The Hexicule Core keeps the tree rooted within the ground, serves as a light beacon for the surrounding area, and is nearly indestructible.
The tree sits at UCC-0, the world's base time zone, making it the geographic and temporal reference point of the entire planet.

More than just a natural wonder, the Oakgnar Grand Tree is a symbol of world unity, representing a place where all four corners of Hetra come together, bound by their differences and their shared connection to the land.
The Sethranian Church was built by one of the Seven Architects, Sethra, back in the Greungerian Era.
People often come here to send wishes and prayers to Queen Eira, as the Religion of Valthoreia is Planet Hetra's main modern religion.
Every year, for a full month during Muhulmber (a 60-day month), festivities, weddings, and world-wide celebrations are held on Rynel.
People come from across Planet Hetra, regardless of their differences, to celebrate the life they were given.
The spirit of the event is simple: set aside the pain and the hardship for a month and enjoy being alive.
Rynel Ruins sits south of both the Oakgnar Districts and New Rynels.
The ruins lead underground and are said to be the exact size of the continent itself in terms of their spread beneath the surface.
Scientists speculate that the Rynel Ruins lead to an underground ancient animal kingdom called The Feathered Dinosaurs.
The entrance is sealed off with a divine seal, and no known force has been able to break through it.
Whether what lies beneath is truly an ancient kingdom, a repository of lost knowledge, or something else entirely, remains one of the great mysteries of Planet Hetra.
Varleqe is a massive supercontinent that is west of all the other continents and almost takes up 1/5th of the globe (if you look on the map).
Varleqe is inhabited by beasts, mythological creatures, demons, and animals.
Direwolves are considered beasts, and Kydel is one of them.
Greenlux Town is located north, beyond the North Mountains.
Greenlux is very close to the border of Varleqe and was considered a thriving town back in the days.
Oldtree Cementery is a small town with its cemetery as its primary attraction.
Smackdab in the center of Varleqe, southeast of the other free towns, Greenside Hills is a city that once was active.
Greenside Hills used to be a tourist attraction for people around the world because of its beautiful architecture that the buildings are built on.
In smaller areas, animals live in a condensed area within their own respective kingdom.
Mountainbearer Ruins is north of the Hidden Plains Ruins.
The Hillside Gate Ruins are filled with lush caves, so there's plenty of animals there.
The Underwater Chambers is hidden under the water off the coast of Varleqe, southeast.
The Gulf of Varleqe was formed from a meteor impact in the past.
Parts of the lands are still here, now known as islands.
The Draxian Sky Church was built by Draxyn, one of The Seven Architects of the Greungerian Era.
Draxday, the sixth day of the Hetranian week and the Friday equivalent, is named in his honor.
Draxyn was the sixth of The Seven Architects to complete his work, and the one who departed most completely from any conventional understanding of what a church was supposed to be.
Historical accounts describe him as visionary and eccentric, an Architect who rarely explained his decisions in terms others found immediately sensible.
The magic required to build and suspend the Draxian Sky Church in the air was unlike anything the other Architects attempted.
The Draxian Sky Church is a massive floating structure, large enough to comfortably accommodate multiple dragons of varying sizes simultaneously.
The structure is built from skystone, a mineral-dense rock found in high-altitude geological formations that Draxyn sourced specifically for its low density relative to its strength.
Entrances are wide open arches, large enough for a dragon to pass through comfortably in flight.
Inside, the main hall is enormous, with a ceiling high enough to allow a large dragon to fully extend its wings.
The most populous dragon species at the Sky Church, with a known population of at least 3,510 individuals distributed across their elemental subtypes.
Magic-descent creatures born of Elemental Magic, each carrying an elemental affinity.
The Draxian Sky Church has no fixed terrestrial location.
The dragons who live there probably prefer it that way.
The Draxian Sky Church is the only one of the seven Architect churches with no human or humanoid clergy, no formal administrative body, and no institutional oversight of any kind.
Of the seven churches, the Draxian Sky Church is the only one that has never touched the ground since the day Draxyn finished building it.
Ancient texts reference the Erbgeroger Flower, but the true origin of both the flower and its barrier has been lost to history.
Surface entrance found at the Euriel Town ruins (Euriel Ruins).
Hethurgism is an ancient martial arts originating in the Greungerian Era.
The closest Earth equivalent would be a combination of Wuxia Arts, Tai-Chi, and Japanese Aikido.
The Eulerian Catalogs houses an extensive collection of magical items: spells, incantations, grimoires, tomes, and artifacts.
Ancient weapons are present, though they are extremely fragile and must not be handled roughly.
Decorative objects include a giant hammer that swings like Mjolnir, and a giant claymore said to have beheaded a giant demon dragon.
The Hynnian Church is built by Hynnia, one of The Seven Architects back in the Greungerian Era.
Hynnia was the first of The Seven Architects to complete a church, earning his place as the namesake for Hynsday, the first day of the Hetranian week.
Little is known about his origins, but historical records from the Greungerian Era describe him as a quiet, deliberate craftsman.
Someone who believed that the beauty of a structure could speak where words could not.

Rather than brute-force shaping stone, Hynnia was said to have listened to the land beneath Eulanis, weaving his magic along the natural ley-lines of the Sandstone Mountains before laying a single foundation.
The Hynnian Church is carved directly into the face of the Sandstone Mountains that surround Eulanis.
The windows are inlaid with translucent amber and citrine crystal panels, casting long warm-toned light across the interior floor during sunrise and midday hours.
Inside, the main hall stretches deep into the mountain, with a high vaulted ceiling reinforced by Hynnia's structural magic.
A large altar sits at the far end of the hall, lit perpetually by a warm amber flame that historians believe was set by Hynnia himself and has never been extinguished.
The church is most closely associated with Gianquisim, the Old Faith, given its construction during the Greungerian Era.
Services are held on Hynsday mornings, which is considered the traditional day of rest and reflection.
Coronations and major civic oaths are traditionally sworn on the church steps.
The Hynnian Church sits in the northern quarter of Eulanis, built against and partially into the Sandstone Mountains.
The city's main road runs past the church's lower steps, making it a natural waypoint for travelers arriving from Endriel to the southeast.
A small order of clergy, known as the Keepers of the First Flame, tend to the church full time.
Named after Iyona, one of The Seven Architects of the Greungerian Era, the Iyonian Churches are unique among the seven.
Iyona was the second of The Seven Architects to complete a church, and she completed it twice.
Historical accounts describe her as restless and ambitious, someone who could not stand the idea of leaving something half-done.

The first of Iyona's churches stands in the Everherk Desert, a vast desert that takes up roughly one-third of the Continent of Lynneria, situated southwest of the country of Nharvenile and west of Riverchnaut.
The nearest major settlements are the cities and towns of Riverchnaut and Nharvenile to the north and east, including the science-fantasy city of Grelladore and the capital Eldreule.
The Everherk Church was built to withstand the extreme conditions of the desert: heat, sandstorms, and the abrasive winds that roll off the dunes.
The structure is low and wide, with a flat, tiered roofline designed to let sand slide off during storms.
The exterior is pale amber with veins of deep rust-red running through the stone, natural mineral patterns Iyona chose to preserve rather than hide, treating them as part of the design.
Inside, the church is cool despite the desert heat, a product of Iyona's enchantments still active millennia later.

The interior walls are lined with shallow geometric carvings, abstract patterns that scholars believe are a visual language derived from an ancient dialect of Ghrenglish, though not all of it has been translated.

Given Lynneria's diverse and technologically advanced culture, the church also attracts scholars from Grelladore and Ironbark who study the ancient carvings on its walls, believing them to contain untranslated lore from the Greungerian Era.
Iyona's second church was built within the Kingdom of Oelen on the Continent of Eulerich, southwest of the Eulan Kingdom.

The Oelen Kingdom is situated in the Oelen Plains, a landscape of open flatland that stretches near the border of Eulerich, with the Cold Rigid Sea to the west and the Oelen Desert at its northern edge.
The church sits near the city of Oelenis, the major city of the Oelen Kingdom, which is home to professions like carpentry, smithing, cartography, and oceanography.
The exterior is deep grey stone quarried from the mineral-rich caves connected to the Rockseige Chasm, the great mining network of the Oelen Kingdom.
The stonework is dense and precise, with the spire capped by a smooth, curved point shaped by Iyona's magic into a seamless taper, with no joints, no seams, just a single unbroken surface.
The interior is darker and more solemn than the Everherk Church.

High narrow windows let in shafts of light that move across the floor as the day progresses, a feature Iyona is believed to have engineered deliberately, so that the light traces a slow arc from east to west, mimicking the path of the sun.
The altar here is carved from a single slab of Oelen ore, its surface naturally striated with silver and dark grey.
The Oelen Church serves as the primary place of worship for the Kingdom of Oelen.
Iyonsday services are well-attended, and the church plays a central civic role in the kingdom, much like the Hynnian Church does in Eulanis.

Given the Oelen Kingdom's strong maritime and mining culture, the church also holds sea-blessing ceremonies, rituals for sailors and ships departing from Oelenis toward the Cold Rigid Sea and the Alarctic Frost.
Iyona is the only Architect whose legacy spans two continents.
Lhavaria, a city that was once on a continent called Lhavia, was a prominent nation during the Greungeria Era.
In the Era of Greungeria, the City of Lhavaria resides on an island near Varleqe, which was once an aspiring city that held ancient technology like Teleportation Crystals, Sea Magic, and of the sort.
Today, the ruins of Lhavaria serve as the capital region for a thriving Merfolk civilization.
The original architecture, though weathered by centuries underwater, remains largely intact, preserved by residual magical enchantments that were woven into the city's construction.
The Merfolk have adapted the ancient structures to their aquatic lifestyle, transforming plazas into coral gardens and repurposing the grand halls as gathering spaces.
The crystals were believed to be attuned to specific locations through a complex ritual involving Sea Magic and elemental harmonization.
Scholars believe that if the Archive could be recovered, it might unlock secrets of magic thought lost forever, including the original methods of creating and programming Teleportation Crystals.
The Oakgnar Grand Tree is a symbolism where all the four corners of Hetra (earth) binds together where people are unified despite absolute differences of each other.
The Oakgnar Tree stands at a whopping height of 5.42 heunix (miles) in height, which is around 8.72 heunix (kilometers) tall.
The entire root system stretches under and beneath the continent of Rynel, which roughly makes the shape of said continent.
The base of the tree is not too wide because the continent of Rynel acts as the support.
The leaves from the tree itself contains mystical properties which makes it harder to study, since most scientists think it protects the tree itself from harm.
You can buy a special compass at local shops to track the tree.
The Oakgnar Grand Tree is directly located at UCC±0, in the center zone of the region.
Every year, for a duration of one month, festivities, weddings, and celebrations are held specifically on Rynel during the month of Griselmber.
In the Ancient Era of Greungeria, the Oakgnar Tree stood there as a navigational system for early settlements and migration within visible reach.
Now, the Valthoreians have dispersed in terms of religious means, but still kept the religion of Valthoreia alive.
The base of the Oakgnar tree's circumference isn't too wide, nor does it take up much space on land.
The Runthian Church was built by Runthia, one of The Seven Architects of the Greungerian Era.
Runthia is the namesake of Runesday, the fourth day of the Hetranian week, the Wednesday equivalent.
Of all the Architect churches, the Runthian Church holds a particularly intimate quality.
Runthia was the fourth of The Seven Architects to complete her work.
Historical accounts describe her as warm and community-minded, someone who did not see sacred architecture as something that should tower over people, but something that should stand among them.
The Runthian Church is built from dark wood and river stone, materials native to Ribbonfelt's surrounding landscape.
The exterior has a low, sloped roofline with wide eaves, designed to shed rain and light snowfall from the nearby ice caps.
The most distinctive feature of the exterior is the lantern row: a series of iron brackets along the front face of the building, each one designed to hold a lit lantern.
On ceremonial nights, the lanterns are all lit simultaneously, and the church front glows in a warm line of light visible from across the village.
Inside, the church is modest in scale but rich in texture.
The wooden ceiling beams are carved with interlocking patterns in a style unique to Varleqe's early settlements.
Rows of simple benches face a stone altar at the far end, and the walls hold shallow carved alcoves where lanterns are kept burning during services.
The overall feeling is one of gathered warmth rather than overwhelming grandeur.
Ribbonfelt is historically known for the SeaLit Lanterns, a tradition where residents gather to send lit lanterns out toward the sea.
The tradition draws from a deep sense of remembrance and release, of honoring things and people that have passed or moved on.
The lantern row on the church's exterior, and the lanterns kept lit within its walls, were designed to echo the SeaLit ceremony in miniature.
On the night of a SeaLit gathering, the Runthian Church serves as the formal starting point: lanterns are blessed at the altar before being carried to the sending grounds.
The lanterns inside are always lit, and the iron brackets outside are always maintained.
The Runthian Church is primarily associated with Gianquisim, the Old Faith, in keeping with its Greungerian Era origins.
Runesday services are held weekly and tend to be small and intimate gatherings, reflecting the village scale of Ribbonfelt itself.
In a continent defined largely by abandonment and ruins, the Runthian Church's continued operation is quietly remarkable.
Ribbonfelt is a town in the northern region of Varleqe, southwest of Greenlux Town and not far from the ice caps to the north.
The Runthian Church sits near the center of Ribbonfelt, on a modest plot facing the town's main open space.
The Wardens keep the interior lanterns lit, lead Runesday services, and organize the SeaLit Lanterns ceremony when the season allows.
The Sethranian Church of Unity was built by Sethra, the seventh and final of The Seven Architects of the Greungerian Era.
Sethraday, the seventh day of the Hetranian week and the Saturday equivalent, is named in his honor.
Sethra was the last of The Seven Architects to complete his work, and the one who had the most time to observe what the others had built before him.
By the time it was his turn, Sethra had a question the others had not explicitly asked: what about everyone?
Historical accounts describe Sethra as reflective and deliberate, someone who spoke carefully and built with the same care.
The Sethranian Church of Unity is the most deliberately composed of all seven Architect churches.
The building is circular in plan, with no front or back face.
Inside, the main hall is open and bright, lit by a ring of high windows that circle the upper walls and flood the interior with light from all directions simultaneously regardless of the time of day.
The Sethranian Church of Unity was intentionally positioned near the Oakgnar Grand Tree, and the relationship between the two is central to understanding what Sethra built.
Together, the tree and the church form a site unlike any other on Hetra: a natural monument and a constructed one, side by side, both pointing to the same truth.
The Sethranian Church of Unity is the only Architect church explicitly designed for all peoples, all races, and all faiths simultaneously.
Representatives from different continents, kingdoms, and races have used the church as neutral territory for negotiations, agreements, and cultural exchanges throughout its history.
During the Oakgnar Grand Festivities, the church is open continuously for the full duration of the month, staffed around the clock by the church's clergy.
Rynel sits at UCC ±0, the baseline of the Universal Celestial Clock, making it the temporal as well as geographic center of Hetra's world.
The Sethranian Church of Unity is tended by the Order of the Seven Arches, a multi-faith, multi-race clergy organization unique among the Architect church orders in its deliberate diversity.
Of all seven Architect churches, the Sethranian Church of Unity is the most visited, the most written about, and the most cited in diplomatic and cultural records across Hetra's history.
Hetrania is home to creatures and animals, and is the first place for Kydel to make home.
Getting here to Hetrania is not easy and very dangerous, for there are bridges that connect from Varleqe to Hetrania.
The wind flow is very strong, so when the bridges sway, it's not a good idea to cross them.
The bridges that connect both places together are very steep and angled very high.
Even though Hetrania is a floating sky continent, it sometimes drifts back towards the seas' surface one every full-moon, when the full-moon shines directly onto the continent.
Long before it became the sky continent it is today, Hetrania was once a piece of the ancient supercontinent of Greungeria.

Greungeria was a massive landmass that nearly covered the whole body of Planet Hetra in its earliest days, a land full of wildlife, prehistoric beasts, direosaurus wolves, dragons, and all manner of living creatures.
Parts of the land of Greungeria had been carved out by Zohl's hand so that it can float in the sky.
Pink like crystals called Hexicules help it stay afloat in the air.
A lesser demon witch named Rachnaea had appeared on the neighboring continent of Varleqe, leeching power from one of the Spirit Wardens and growing stronger with every passing hour.

A new bed of clouds formed near the mountain elevation once the continent reached its height, giving the region a fresh layer of air quality and a constantly shifting atmosphere that makes the place feel unlike anywhere else on Hetra.
After the land was secured in the sky, Zohl manifested a chain bridge hanging from Hetrania down to Varleqe.
The bridge sways hard in the high-altitude winds, it angles at a steep incline, and crossing it feels less like walking a path and more like climbing a ladder that does not want to stay still.
Rachnaea, who could not fly at the time, could not follow.
The bridge remains as treacherous as the day Zohl made it.
On Hetrania, there are gate ruins that lead to a divine cave underground called the Spiritqual.
The Spiritqual was built by Zohl and the Spirit Wardens.
The cave itself was carved out by Zohl long before the continent ever left the surface of Hetra.
The Skypeak Obelisk is the center of attraction in the city of Grelladore, in Nharvenile, a country north of Riverchnaut.
The Skypeak Obelisk serves as a Fantasy-Video game-like system where you can farm actual ExP Points to help better and improve your powers, including gold.
The building itself has over millions of windows that are made out of hexicules, which is stronger than diamond and a lot of other materials.
Hexicules are magic crystals that help serve as a fundamental core when it comes to buildings or inventions.
The building itself is made out of indestructible metal called Hardwood-Lucid, which is made by combining Lyecerium crystals and Norrane Hardwood Trees together.
The Skypeak Obelisk is unlike any other attraction on Planet Hetra.
A free guided tour is available to all newcomers, led by a compact robot tour guide that takes guests on a tram-like ride through the building's vast interior.
The remaining 100 floors serve as the Obelisk's control deck.
Domains are one of the most popular challenge features within the Obelisk.
Highly contested or long-unbeaten domains can accumulate enormous reward pools over time, making them prime targets for skilled adventurers.
The Obelisk's housing system spans every active floor, each with a distinct seasonal theme.
Players can purchase, customize, and even take their housing with them.
Certain properties can be miniaturized into a magic-laced container for portable travel outside the Obelisk entirely, and resized by a magic user at will.
Whether through domains, PVP, monster hunting, or sparring in training fields, every action within the Obelisk can yield XP.
A single hexicule energy can regenerate at insane and excessive speeds, so recharging isn\u2019t an only option.
Hexicules that are modified into batteries lose 30\u201350% of their charge.
Elenia has no gender, but considers herself female due to Elena's inheritance.
A waterfall that stands so high, the water that falls glows a very fluorescent blue color, due to different layers of atmospheric pressure.
At a whopping height of 3,833 meters (12,578 feet) tall, it is the highest earth-made structure in the entire world.
The glow intensifies at dusk and dawn, creating an ethereal spectacle that can be seen for miles across the northern landscape.
Travelers must pass through Oldtree Cemetery and venture deep into the northern mountains, where direwolves, demons, and other dangerous beasts roam freely.
At the waterfall's base lies the Varleqian Basin, a massive crystalline pool that stretches for nearly half a mile in diameter.
Rare Lumimoss grows on the rocks, glowing faintly in harmony with the waterfall.
Deeragons, ethereal creatures with translucent antlers, are often spotted drinking from the basin at dawn.
The waterfall was first documented by the ancient Varleqian civilization over 3,000 years ago.
Ruins near the peak suggest there was once a temple complex dedicated to water deities, though much of it has crumbled into the abyss.
Few have successfully climbed to the waterfall's source at the mountain peak.
Scholars debate whether the waterfall's placement as a Wonder is purely for its physical grandeur, or if there's a deeper, magical significance connected to the ancient world's power structure.
The Yhursian Demon Church was built by Yhursa, one of The Seven Architects of the Greungerian Era.
Yhursday, the fifth day of the Hetranian week and the Thursday equivalent, is named in her honor.
Yhursa was the fifth of The Seven Architects to complete her work, and by far the most unconventional.
Historical accounts are sparse on Yhursa's personal history, but what exists describes her as fearless and principled, someone who believed that sacred architecture should not exclude based on race.
Yhursa is said to have navigated the territorial tensions of Varleqe's demon communities with a quiet, unshakeable confidence, earning enough trust from them to build among them.
“Every soul deserves a place to stand and something to stand for.”
The Yhursian Demon Church does not look like the other Architect churches.
The exterior walls are the original ruin stonework, reinforced and reshaped by Yhursa's structural magic.
The entrance is marked by two large carved stone pillars Yhursa added herself, etched in Varnæn, the demonic dialect of Ghrenglish.
The walls are rough-hewn and dark, lit by a network of iron torch brackets Yhursa enchanted to burn indefinitely with a deep red flame.
The floor is polished smooth, a stark contrast to the raw stone walls, and bears a large engraved sigil at the center believed to be a Greungerian-era symbol of sanctuary.
The altar at the far end is carved from volcanic black stone, inset with veins of deep red mineral that catch the torchlight.
The Yhursian Demon Church does not align neatly with any of the four major faiths of Hetra.
In practice, the church has served as a neutral spiritual ground for the demons of Varleqe: a place to gather for rites of passage, territorial truces, and communal ceremonies.
Yhursday is observed here not through structured liturgy but through gathering itself.
One of the Yhursian Church's most significant and practical functions has always been as a neutral zone during territorial disputes.
Attacking or fighting within the church's boundaries has been considered a serious violation of demon cultural law since the Greungerian Era.
The Yhursian Demon Church is built into one of Varleqe's many ruin sites, in the interior region of the supercontinent where demons have historically concentrated their presence.
Varleqe is a continent where most human settlement has declined or collapsed.
The church sits in a demon-territorial zone, which means access for non-demon visitors is difficult and requires either an invitation or significant combat capability.
The Yhursian Demon Church is the most difficult of the seven Architect churches to access and the least documented.
Of the seven churches, the Yhursian Demon Church is the one that has changed the least since Yhursa built it.
